title: Platform degradation matrix — upstream probes (CLIProxyAPI v7.3.4, commit 8335eac731946bd4eff18f500653f93736df53d6)
notes: All cases are RECORDABLE-LOCALLY unless marked FIXTURE-DEFERRED; none require real provider credentials.
Default base URL: http://127.0.0.1:18317 (oracle container; run/config.yaml template unchanged unless a case says otherwise).
Management key: 'oracle-mgmt-key-1' (Authorization: Bearer or X-Management-Key). Client API key: 'oracle-local-key-1'.
Sequence cases (S7-02, S7-08, S7-13, S7-14, S7-15) must run in order on one container; S7-08 continues from S7-07 state.
S7-13 additionally publishes container port 54545 (docker run -p 127.0.0.1:54545:54545).
Fixture layout per reports/oracle/BOOTSTRAP.md RECIPES: meta.yaml / request.http / downstream.md / upstream.jsonl / mock-response.json; for multi-step cases use downstream-<step>.md.

Dynamic fields must be listed in meta.yaml dynamic_fields (state values, PKCE code_challenge in URLs, log line contents, latest-timestamp, next-cursor, Sec-WebSocket-Key/Accept, UnixNano states, container paths).
Dynamic-fields hygiene (adversary N9): meta.yaml dynamic_fields must list every environment-dependent byte exhaustively (ports, timestamps, states, log contents, container paths).

cases.title: ws-handshake-rejected-no-upgrade
cases.purpose: Demonstrate that upstream registers GET /v1/ws and — with the oracle config (ws-auth unset) — requires an API key there: the config loader presets ws-auth=true, so a plain unauthenticated GET returns 401 Missing API key. The gorilla 400 upgrade-rejection is covered by S7-02 (explicit ws-auth false, or valid key).

requests.note: RECORDED FACT: ws-auth unset => auth REQUIRED (internal/config/config_load.go presets true); expect 401 {"error":"Missing API key"} with the CORS block. A 400 'Bad Request' does NOT occur here.

record: status + response headers + exact body bytes (expect 400 text/plain 'Bad Request' + Sec-Websocket-Version: 13 + gin CORS block)
cases.auxiliary_evidence: docker logs: no ws-related lines expected

cases.title: ws-auth-gating-toggle
cases.purpose: Demonstrate the ws-auth switch: management key gates it; enabling it makes /v1/ws require an API key; disabling re-opens it. This is the observable used by the CPA-Edge degraded-runtime contract (auth errors precede the 501).

requests.note: PUT true matches the already-active default (loader preset); watcher reload also fires

record: each numbered exchange: status + headers + body; also capture docker logs around the toggle (ws-auth reload / session termination lines if any)

cases.title: ws-wrong-method-404-and-options-cors
cases.purpose: Confirm R-404 semantics on the /v1/ws route: POST is 404 with empty body (only GET is registered), OPTIONS is auto-answered 204 with CORS.
record: both exchanges: status + headers + body bytes

cases.title: ws-upgrade-101-handshake
cases.purpose: Prove the inbound upgrade path works upstream: a minimal stdlib WebSocket handshake (no session protocol use) returns 101 with a correct Sec-WebSocket-Accept; the server then registers a synthetic runtime-only aistudio credential. This is exactly the capability vercel lacks.

requests.detail:
python3 stdlib (socket+base64+hashlib): open TCP to 127.0.0.1:18317; send 'GET /v1/ws HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:18317
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: <base64 16 bytes>
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13

'; read full 101 response head; compute base64(SHA1(key+'258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11')) and compare with Sec-WebSocket-Accept; then send a close frame (opcode 0x88, payload 2 bytes 03 E8) and close.

record: full 101 response head bytes; computed accept value; note that the server sends no message before close (it waits for client JSON)
cases.auxiliary_evidence: docker logs must show 'websocket provider connected: aistudio-<16 alnum chars>' during the probe window

cases.title: proxy-url-config-accepted-echo
cases.purpose: Demonstrate proxy-url config acceptance and visibility: management CRUD round-trip + config echo. No credential is used; the feature is visible through its config surface.
record: each exchange status+headers+body; for step 3 record the full config JSON once (dynamic fields: secret-key hash, model lists)

cases.title: api-call-proxy-transport-engaged
cases.purpose: Prove the proxy transport is ENGAGED, not just stored: a management api-call through a dead socks5 port fails with 502 while the same URL direct succeeds; ftp:// is rejected as invalid proxy_url. This is the upstream behavior CPA-Edge degrades to 501 on serverless runtimes.

requests.expect: 502 {"error":"request failed"} (socks5 dial to dead port 9 fails; proves transport engaged)
200 status_code 200 (explicit direct bypass works, same as control)

record: all four exchanges; upstream.jsonl = the two mock hits from steps 1 and 4 (mock logs each incoming request)
cases.config_setup: mock_openai.py running on host port 18999; no config change needed

cases.title: plugins-config-accepted-visible
cases.purpose: Demonstrate the plugins config surface is accepted and visible after an EXTERNAL config file edit (also exercises hot-reload): plugins.enabled=true + a configured instance show up in GET /v0/management/plugins with registered=false (no binary present).

requests.detail:
append to run/config.yaml (host file edit, server NOT restarted):
plugins:
  enabled: true
  dir: "plugins"
  configs:
    example:
      enabled: true
      priority: 1
      mode: "safe"
then sleep 2s for the 150ms-debounced watcher

record: plugins list JSON verbatim; docker logs: the config-reload lines (config file changed / config successfully reloaded)
cases.config_setup: file edit as described; note the server rewrites config.yaml (comment/format normalization) — record the post-reload file hash or a diff in meta

cases.title: plugins-config-ops-and-delete
cases.purpose: Demonstrate the plugin config mutation surface that CPA-Edge keeps wire-compatible while never loading anything: PATCH enabled, GET/PUT config object, DELETE plugin. Also captures the 409 'plugin_delete_requires_restart' preconditions are unreachable without a loaded plugin.

requests.expect: 200 config object with enabled:false (plus priority/mode preserved)
200 list; example entry configured:true, registered:false, effective_enabled:false

record: all exchanges; config file final state (plugins block remains with empty configs)
cases.config_setup: requires S7-07 plugins block present first (sequence after S7-07 on same container)

cases.title: logs-endpoints-disabled-400
cases.purpose: Demonstrate the logs API surface and its gating: with logging-to-file=false (default), GET and DELETE /v0/management/logs both return 400 {"error":"logging to file disabled"}. Size-limit config keys are accepted and echoed.

cases.title: logs-enabled-lines-and-clear
cases.purpose: Demonstrate file logging enabled: the toggle persists, GET /v0/management/logs returns the rotating-file log content shape (lines/line-count/latest-timestamp/next-cursor), DELETE clears rotated files with a JSON success body.

requests.expect: 200 {"lines":[...up to 3 log lines...],"line-count":N,"latest-timestamp":<epoch>,"next-cursor":"<string>"} — record exact JSON shape; line CONTENTS are dynamic (timestamps, ports)
200 with RECORDED byte order {"message":"Logs cleared successfully","removed":N,"success":true} (N=0 on a fresh container; do not reorder keys)

record: all exchanges; dynamic_fields: line contents, latest-timestamp, next-cursor
step 3 response key order as recorded: {"latest-timestamp":...,"line-count":N,"lines":[...]}
cases.config_setup: run/config.yaml; RECORDED FACT: log files materialize under the AUTH DIR (<auth-dir>/logs/main.log, host: run3/run/auths/logs/), NOT next to config.yaml. Per-request error-*.log dumps appear there even while logging-to-file=false (separate feature, error-logs-max-files retention) — capture samples as aux artifacts.

cases.title: oauth-callback-routes-static
cases.purpose: Demonstrate the provider-redirect callback routes served on the MAIN server port (these are plain HTTP and stay EQUIVALENT on every runtime): anthropic/codex/antigravity always answer 200 with a fixed HTML page; the devin variants validate parameters. No auth is required.

requests.expect: 200 text/html; charset=utf-8 with the exact fixed HTML page (title 'Authentication successful', auto-close script)
200 same fixed HTML (no pending session: file write is attempted only when state matches a pending session; response is identical)
400 {"error":"invalid or expired OAuth callback"} (no pending session)

record: all exchanges with exact body bytes (the HTML is a fixed constant — byte-compare)

cases.title: mgmt-oauth-session-surface-errors
cases.purpose: Demonstrate the OAuth session registry surface that stays EQUIVALENT on serverless (pure HTTP, state-based): /v0/management/oauth-callback GET+POST error ladder and /get-auth-status + DELETE /oauth-session for an unknown state. All paths deterministic without any credential.

requests.expect: 400 {"status":"error","error":"state is required"} (NO management key needed: route is outside the mgmt auth group)
200 {"status":"ok"} (empty state) — note: record BOTH with and without the management key to document auth requirements

cases.title: anthropic-auth-url-forwarder
cases.purpose: Demonstrate the localhost callback forwarder — the exact serverless-impossible feature: GET anthropic-auth-url?is_webui=1 returns 200 with a URL whose redirect is localhost:54545, binds 0.0.0.0:54545, and that listener answers 302 -> http://127.0.0.1:18317/anthropic/callback forwarding query params. Deterministic: the redirect is NOT followed, so no code is delivered and no external call happens.

requests.expect: 302 Found; Location: http://127.0.0.1:18317/anthropic/callback?code=oracle-demo-code&state=<state>; Cache-Control: no-store — curl WITHOUT -L so the redirect is not followed
requests.note: claude redirect_uri is http://localhost:54545/callback (internal/auth/claude/anthropic_auth.go); the forwarder answers ANY path. The 302 Location embeds the SERVER'S CONFIG PORT (worker-3 stack: 8397; not a fixed constant). curl WITHOUT -L so the redirect is not followed. Container must publish 54545 (worker-3 used host 24545->54545).

requests.expect: 200 {"status":"wait"} (session still pending: the forwarded callback target was never fetched)

record: all exchanges; dynamic_fields: state (32 hex), url (PKCE code_challenge + state embedded)
cases.auxiliary_evidence: docker logs: 'callback forwarder for anthropic listening on 0.0.0.0:54545' and later 'callback forwarder on port 54545 stopped'; DO NOT follow the 302 (keeps the case offline-safe)

cases.title: config-hot-reload-external-edit
cases.purpose: Demonstrate the file-watcher feature vercel/cloudflare lose: an EXTERNAL edit of config.yaml (never via the API) is picked up live without restart. Add a second API key, observe it in the management echo, then remove it and observe removal.

requests.detail: on the host, edit run/config.yaml: change the api-keys list from ['oracle-local-key-1'] to ['oracle-local-key-1','oracle-hot-key-2'] (keep all other content identical); sleep 2s

requests.expect: 200 with the current model list — content is environment-specific (the recording template wires 8 providers; NOT an empty data array). The S7 claim is only: the hot-added key authenticates.

record: all exchanges; docker logs: 'config file changed, reloading: /CLIProxyAPI/config.yaml' + 'config successfully reloaded' + config-change detail lines
cases.config_setup: run/config.yaml; fresh container recommended so the two file edits are the only mutations

cases.title: auth-dir-watcher-credential-file
cases.purpose: Demonstrate the auth-dir half of the watcher: dropping a syntactically valid (fake, non-functional) OAuth JSON file into the auth directory hot-registers a credential; deleting it hot-removes it. The transcript also documents upstream's parsing tolerance.

requests.detail: create run/auths/oracle-fake-kimi.json (host-side, auth dir is mounted) with body: {"type":"kimi","access_token":"oracle-fake-token","refresh_token":"oracle-fake-refresh","token_type":"Bearer","expired":"2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"}; sleep 2s

requests.expect: 200; the fake kimi file IS accepted and hot-registered (recorded: auth-files entry with provider kimi, account_type oauth, quota.signals{}, recent_requests buckets)

record: all exchanges + final auth-files list shape; docker logs: watcher auth add/remove lines (e.g. 'provider added'), and any 'skipping auth file' warning if the fake file is rejected
cases.config_setup: run/config.yaml as-is; auth dir mount already present

cases.title: device-flow-auth-url-shapes
cases.purpose: Document the device user-code flow UX surface that remains available on serverless (xai/meta/kimi-auth-url hit vendor device-authorize endpoints and return a URL + user_code without any inbound callback). Response shape from source: 200 {"status":"ok","url":...,"state":"<prefix>-<UnixNano>","flow":"device","user_code":...,"expires_in":N}.
cases.defer_reason: CREDENTIALED-ONLY: starts REAL device authorizations at vendor endpoints (api.x.ai / api.meta.ai / api.kimi.com) with dynamic user_code/url/state; completion requires a live account. Specified from upstream source (internal/api/handlers/management/auth_files_provider_oauth.go); record only if the orchestrator explicitly authorizes live vendor probes. The 501-free classification (device flows are platform-independent) is source-based, not golden-based.
